explain.say: Drop a ball and it falls. Earth's gravity pulls everything down. So why does the Moon, hanging up in the sky, not come crashing down on us? Here is the surprising answer: it is falling, all the time! Let us see how.

faq.q: What keeps the Moon in orbit?
faq.a: Earth's gravity pulls the Moon inwards, while its sideways speed carries it along. Together they make a curved orbit.

faq.q: Why doesn't the Moon fly away?
faq.a: Gravity keeps pulling it towards Earth, bending its path. Without gravity it would carry on in a straight line into space.
Yes. It falls towards Earth all the time, but it moves sideways so fast that it keeps missing.

faq.q: Why do astronauts float on the space station?
faq.a: They are not free of gravity. They and the station are falling round Earth together, so they float relative to it.
asks: Is there no gravity in space?

faq.q: How fast must a satellite go to stay in orbit?
faq.a: Close to Earth, about 7.8 kilometres per second. Higher orbits need less speed.

facts: The Moon orbits Earth at about 1 km/s, taking about 27.3 days per orbit.
The International Space Station travels at about 7.7 km/s and orbits roughly every 90 minutes.
